bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷六十五 唐書41: 列傳17 李建及 石君立 高行珪 張廷裕 王思同 索自通
title.en: Volume 65 Book of Later Tang 41: Biographies 17 - Li Jianji, Shi Junli, Gao Xinggui, Zhang Tingyu, Wang Sitong, Suo Zitong
title.raw: 卷六十五 唐書41: 列傳17 李建及 石君立 高行珪 張廷裕 王思同 索自通 Volume 65 Book of Later Tang 41: Biographies 17 - Li Jianji, Shi Junli, Gao Xinggui, Zhang Tingyu, Wang Sitong, Suo Zitong

sentences.zh: 李建及，許州人。

translations.literal: Li Jianji was a native of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianji came from Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本姓王，父質。

translations.literal: His original surname was Wang; his father's name was Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was born Wang; his father was named Zhi.

sentences.zh: 建及少事李罕之為紀綱，光啟中，罕之謁武皇於晉陽，因選部下驍勇者百人以獻，建及在籍中。

translations.literal: In his youth Jianji served Li Hanzhi as a camp officer. In the Guangqi era, Hanzhi called on the Martial Emperor at Jinyang and thereupon selected a hundred fierce warriors from his subordinates to present; Jianji was on the roster.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Jianji served Li Hanzhi as a camp officer. During the Guangqi reign, Hanzhi visited the Martial Emperor at Jinyang and presented a hundred of his bravest followers; Jianji was among them.

sentences.zh: 後以功署牙職，典義兒軍，及賜姓名。

translations.literal: Later, for merit he was appointed to a yamen post, directed the Foster Sons Army, and was granted a surname and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: He later earned a staff appointment, took charge of the Foster Sons Army, and received the imperial gift of surname and given name.

sentences.zh: 天祐七年，改匡衛軍都校。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou he was made commander of the Kuangwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou year 7 he was promoted to commander of the Kuangwei Army.

sentences.zh: 柏鄉之役，汴將韓追周德威至高邑南野河上，鎮、定兵扼橋道，韓選精兵先奪之。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Baixiang, the Bian general Han pursued Zhou Dewei to the south of Gaoyi on the Ye River; the Zhen and Ding troops held the bridge road, and Han chose elite soldiers to seize it first.
translations.idiomatic: At Baixiang, a Bian commander named Han pressed Zhou Dewei to the Ye River south of Gaoyi. Zhen and Ding forces blocked the bridge, and Han sent picked troops to seize it first.

sentences.zh: 莊宗登高而望，鎮、定兵將衄，謂建及曰：「如賊過橋，則勢不可遏，卿計若何？

translations.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong climbed high to look; the Zhen and Ding troops were about to break, and he said to Jianji, "If the enemy cross the bridge, their momentum cannot be stopped—what is your plan?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong took a vantage point and saw the Zhen and Ding lines buckling. He asked Jianji, "If they get across that bridge we cannot hold them—what do you propose?

sentences.zh: 」建及於部選士二百，挺槍大噪，禦汴軍，卻之於橋下。

translations.literal: " Jianji chose two hundred men from his command, brandished spears with a great shout, met the Bian army, and drove them back below the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " Jianji picked two hundred men, charged with leveled spears and a thunderous yell, met the Bian troops head-on, and forced them back from the bridge.

sentences.zh: 二月，王師攻魏，魏人夜出犯我營，建及設伏待之，扼其歸路，盡殪之。

translations.literal: In the second month the royal army attacked Wei; the Wei men came out by night to strike our camp. Jianji set an ambush, blocked their line of retreat, and slaughtered them to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the imperial army besieged Wei. Wei forces raided the camp at night; Jianji laid an ambush, cut off their retreat, and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩之營莘縣，月餘不出，忽一旦縱兵攻鎮、定之營，軍中騰亂，建及率銀槍勁兵千人赴之，擊敗汴軍，追奔至其壘。

translations.literal: Liu Xun had camped at Shen County for more than a month without coming out; suddenly one day he loosed his troops to attack the Zhen and Ding camp. The army was thrown into turmoil; Jianji led a thousand stalwarts of the Silver Spear corps to the spot, defeated the Bian army, and pursued them to their ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun had sat at Shen County for over a month, then suddenly struck the Zhen and Ding encampment and threw the lines into chaos. Jianji rushed a thousand Silver Spear veterans to the fight, routed the Bian army, and chased them back to their walls.

sentences.zh: 元城之戰，建及首陷其陣，授天雄軍教練使。

translations.literal: In the battle at Yuancheng, Jianji was first to break their formation and was made drill instructor of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuancheng he was the first through the enemy line and was appointed drill instructor of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 八月，遷遼州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to be prefect of Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made prefect of Liao.

sentences.zh: 十四年，從擊契丹於幽州，破之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the campaign against the Khitan at Youzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he joined the expedition against the Khitan at Youzhou and routed them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，從攻楊劉，自寅至午，汴軍嬰城拒守，建及自負葭葦堙塹，率先登梯，遂拔之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he followed the attack on Yangliu; from the hour yin to the hour wu the Bian army clung to the city in defense. Jianji shouldered reed bundles to fill the moat, was first up the scaling ladder, and the place was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he took part in the assault on Yangliu. From dawn to midday the defenders held the walls; Jianji packed the ditch with reed bundles, led the climb, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 胡柳之役，前軍逗撓，際晚，汴軍登土山，建及一戰奪之。

translations.literal: In the battle at Huliu the vanguard hung back; toward evening the Bian army seized a hill. Jianji seized it back in a single clash.
translations.idiomatic: At Huliu the forward units stalled, and by evening the Bian held a hilltop. Jianji retook it in one fight.

sentences.zh: 莊宗欲收軍，詰朝合戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong wished to withdraw the army and join battle at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong wanted to pull the army in and renew the fight at daybreak.

sentences.zh: 建及橫槊當前，曰：「賊大將已亡，乘此易擊，王但登山，觀臣破賊！

translations.literal: Jianji set his spear across the front and said, "The enemy's great general is already dead; press this moment while they are easy to strike. Your Majesty need only climb the hill and watch your servant break the foe!
translations.idiomatic: Jianji planted his spear before the line and said, "Their commander is dead—this is the moment to hit them. Your Majesty, take the hill and watch me break them!

sentences.zh: 」即引銀槍效節大呼奮擊，三軍增氣，由是王師復振，以功授檢校司空、魏博內外衙都將。

translations.literal: " He thereupon led the Silver Spear picked troops in a great shout and fierce charge; the three armies took heart, and thus the royal army rallied. For merit he was made acting Minister of Works and commander of the inner and outer yamen of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the Silver Spear guard in a roaring charge; morale surged across the army and the imperial line steadied again. For this he received the acting title Minister of Works and command of Weibo's inner and outer yamen.

sentences.zh: 十六年，汴將賀瑰攻德勝南城，以戰船十餘艘，竹笮維之，扼斷津路，王師不得渡。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Bian general He Gui attacked the south city of Desheng. With more than ten war junks linked by bamboo chains he choked the crossing; the royal army could not ford.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the Bian commander He Gui besieged Desheng's south citadel. He moored a dozen warships with bamboo hawsers and blocked the ford, so the imperial army could not cross.

sentences.zh: 城中矢石將盡，守城將氏延賞危急，莊宗令積帛軍門，召能破賊船者。

translations.literal: Arrows and stones in the city were nearly spent; the defender Shi Yanshang was in extremity. The Emperor Zhuangzong piled cloth at the camp gate and called for whoever could break the enemy ships.
translations.idiomatic: Missiles inside the walls were almost gone and the commander Shi Yanshang was desperate. Zhuangzong heaped cloth rewards at the gate and asked who could smash the enemy fleet.

sentences.zh: 津人有馬破龍者，能水遊，乃令往見延賞，延賞言：「危窘極矣，所爭晷刻。

translations.literal: A man of the ford district named Ma Polong, who could swim, was sent to see Yanshang. Yanshang said, "The peril is extreme; what is contested is a matter of moments.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Ma Polong, a local man skilled in the water, to Yanshang, who said, "We are at the breaking point—every moment counts.

sentences.zh: 」時棹船滿河，流矢雨集，建及被重鎧，執槊呼曰：「豈有一衣帶水，縱賊如此！

translations.literal: " At that time oared boats filled the river and flying arrows fell like rain. Jianji wore heavy armor, grasped his spear, and shouted, "How can we let the foe run riot across a strip of water no wider than a belt!
translations.idiomatic: " The river swarmed with boats and arrows fell like rain. Jianji in heavy armor gripped his spear and cried, "Will we let them strut across a river we could wade?

sentences.zh: 」乃以二船實甲士，皆短兵持斧，徑抵梁之戰艦，斧其笮；

translations.literal: " He then loaded two boats with armored men, all with short weapons and axes, and drove straight at the Liang war junks to chop through the bamboo links;
translations.idiomatic: " He sent two boats packed with armored men bearing short axes straight at the Liang ships to cut the bamboo hawsers;

sentences.zh: 又令上流具甕，積薪其上，順流縱火，以攻其艦。

translations.literal: he also ordered jars prepared upstream, piled fuel on them, and sent them downstream afire to attack the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: upstream he had jars loaded with fuel set adrift ablaze against the fleet.

sentences.zh: 須臾，煙焰騰熾，梁軍斷纜而遁；

translations.literal: In a moment smoke and flame rose fiercely; the Liang army cut their cables and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Soon smoke and flame towered; the Liang crews cut loose and fled;

sentences.zh: 建及乃入南城，賀瑰解圍而去。

translations.literal: Jianji then entered the south city, and He Gui lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji entered the south city, and He Gui broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，與汴將王瓚戰於戚城，建及傷手，莊宗解禦衣金帶賜之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he fought the Bian general Wang Zan at Weicheng; Jianji was wounded in the hand, and the Emperor Zhuangzong removed his own imperial robe and gold belt to bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month he fought Wang Zan at Weicheng and took a hand wound; Zhuangzong gave him his own court robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 建及有膽氣，慷慨不群，臨陣鞠旅，意氣橫壯，自莊宗至魏州，建及都總內外衙銀槍效節帳前親軍，善於撫禦，所得賞賜，皆分給部下，絕甘分少，頗洽軍情。

translations.literal: Jianji had courage and an uncommonly generous spirit; when he drilled the ranks on campaign his bearing was towering. From the time the Emperor Zhuangzong reached Weizhou, Jianji had overall charge of the Silver Spear picked guard before the imperial tent in the inner and outer yamen. He was skilled at comforting and controlling men; whatever rewards he received he divided among his subordinates, refusing the sweet portion for himself and taking the lesser share, and thus won the troops' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji was bold and open-handed; on the field his presence rallied the ranks. After Zhuangzong reached Weizhou, Jianji commanded the Silver Spear guard in the inner and outer yamen. He knew how to win soldiers—every bounty went to his men, never to his own purse—and the command loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 又累立戰功，雄勇冠絕，雌劣者忌讒之。

translations.literal: He also piled up battle achievements and stood foremost in valor; the timid and base envied and slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: His battle record was unmatched, and weaker men whispered against him.

sentences.zh: 時宦官韋令圖監建及軍，每於莊宗前言：「建及以家財驟施，其趨向誌意不小，不可令典衙兵。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Wei Lingtu supervised Jianji's army and repeatedly said before the Emperor Zhuangzong, "Jianji lavishes his family wealth in sudden gifts; his aims and ambitions are no small matter—he must not be allowed to command the yamen troops.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wei Lingtu oversaw his command and kept telling Zhuangzong, "Jianji showers his own money on the troops—his ambitions are larger than they look. Do not leave the yamen guard in his hands.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗因猜之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor Zhuangzong therefore grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong began to doubt him.

sentences.zh: 建及性既忠藎，雖知讒構，不改其操。

translations.literal: Jianji's nature was loyal and earnest; though he knew of the slanderous plots, he did not alter his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji was loyal by nature; knowing the plots against him, he did not change how he served.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，授代州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year he was made prefect of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 17 he was appointed prefect of Dai.

sentences.zh: 八月，與李存審赴河中，解同州之圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he went with Li Cunshen to the Hezhong region and lifted the siege of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he joined Li Cunshen at Hezhong and relieved Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 建及少遇禍亂，久從戰陣，矢石所中，肌無完膚，後有功見疑，私心憤鬱。

translations.literal: Jianji had met calamity early, followed the battle lines for long years, and been struck by arrows and stones until no patch of flesh on his body was whole. Later, though he had merit, he was met with suspicion and nursed private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He had grown up in chaos and spent years under fire until his body was a map of scars. When merit only brought suspicion, he brooded in private.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒於太原，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In that year he died at Taiyuan, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at Taiyuan at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 石君立，趙州昭慶人也，亦謂之石家財。

translations.literal: Shi Junli was a native of Zhaoping in Zhao Prefecture and was also called Shi Jiacai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Junli came from Zhaoping in Zhao Prefecture and was also known as Shi Jiacai.

sentences.zh: 初事代州刺史李克柔，後隸李嗣昭為牙校，曆典諸軍。

translations.literal: He first served the Dai prefect Li Kerou, then came under Li Sizhao as a yamen officer and successively directed various armies.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Li Kerou, prefect of Dai, then joined Li Sizhao's staff and held a series of army commands.

sentences.zh: 夾城之役，君立每出挑戰，壞汴軍柵壘，俘擒而還。

translations.literal: In the Jiacheng campaign Junli would go out each day to offer challenge, break the Bian army's palisades and ramparts, and return with captives.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiacheng siege he daily rode out to challenge the enemy, tore their stockades, and came back with prisoners.

sentences.zh: 八年，與汴軍戰於龍化園，敗之，獲其大將卜渥以獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he fought the Bian army at Longhua Garden, defeated them, and presented their great general Bu Wo.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he met the Bian at Longhua Garden, routed them, and sent up their general Bu Wo.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭每出征，俾君立為前鋒，敵人畏之。

translations.literal: Whenever Sizhao went on campaign he made Junli the vanguard; the enemy feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao always put Junli in the van on campaign, and foes learned to dread him.

sentences.zh: 王檀之逼晉陽也，城中無備，安金全驅市人以登陴，保聚不完。

translations.literal: When Wang Tan pressed Taiyuan the city had no preparations; An Jinquan drove townspeople up onto the battlements, but the defenses were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tan threatened Taiyuan the city was unprepared; An Jinquan pressed townsfolk onto the walls, but the defenses were still patchwork.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗在魏博，救應不暇，人心危懼，嗣昭遣君立率五百騎，自上黨朝發暮至。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor Zhuangzong was in Weibo and could not spare relief; hearts were fearful. Sizhao sent Junli with five hundred horsemen, who set out from Shangdang in the morning and arrived at evening.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was tied down in Weibo and could not send help; panic spread. Sizhao dispatched Junli with five hundred cavalry from Shangdang—they left at dawn and reached Taiyuan by nightfall.

sentences.zh: 王檀遊軍扼汾橋，君立一戰敗之，徑至城下，馳突斬擊，出入如神，大呼曰：「昭義侍中大軍至矣！

translations.literal: Wang Tan's patrols held the Fen Bridge; Junli defeated them in one fight, went straight to the wall, and charged in slashing strikes, in and out like a spirit, shouting, "The Grand Mentor of Zhaoyi and his great army have arrived!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan's scouts held the Fen Bridge; Junli smashed them in one clash, raced to the gates, and wheeled through the ranks like a demon, shouting, "The Zhaoyi Grand Mentor's host is here!

sentences.zh: 」是夜入城，與安金全等分出諸門擊殺於外，遲明，梁軍敗走。

translations.literal: " That night he entered the city; with An Jinquan and others he sent men out through the gates to strike and kill outside. At dawn the Liang army broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " That night he entered the city. He and An Jinquan split sorties through every gate; by dawn the Liang line broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 十七年，將兵屯德勝。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he led troops to garrison Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he garrisoned Desheng with his troops.

sentences.zh: 時汴軍自滑州轉餉以給楊村寨，莊宗親率騎軍於河外，循岸而上，邀擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the Bian army turned supplies from Huazhou to feed the stockade at Yang Village; the Emperor Zhuangzong personally led cavalry along the riverbank upstream to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian were shipping grain from Huazhou to Yang Village; Zhuangzong led cavalry along the north bank to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 汴人距楊村五十里，於河曲潘張村築壘以貯軍儲，莊宗令諸軍攻之。

translations.literal: The Bian men, fifty li from Yang Village, built a stockade at Panzhang Village on a bend of the river to store military provisions; the Emperor Zhuangzong ordered the armies to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li from Yang Village the Bian built a depot at Panzhang on the river bend; Zhuangzong ordered a general assault.

sentences.zh: 汴人設伏於要路，逆戰偽敗，王師乘之，蹙入壘門，梁伏兵起，因與血戰。

translations.literal: The Bian set an ambush on the vital road, met in battle with a feigned defeat; the royal army pressed them and was crowded into the stockade gate. Liang hidden troops rose, and there was a bloody fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian laid an ambush on the road, fought a sham retreat, and drew the imperial troops into the gate; hidden Liang units rose and the melee turned bloody.

sentences.zh: 君立與鎮州大將王釗陷入賊壘，時諸將部校陷賊者十餘人，君立被執，送於汴。

translations.literal: Junli and the Zhenzhou great general Wang Zhao fell into the enemy stockade. At that time more than ten commanders and officers of various generals were trapped; Junli was seized and sent to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Junli and the Zhen commander Wang Zhao were trapped inside. More than ten officers were taken with them; Junli was sent to the Liang capital.

sentences.zh: 梁祖素知其驍勇，欲用之為將，械而下獄。

translations.literal: The Liang Founder had long known his fierceness and wished to use him as a general; he was shackled and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu of Liang knew his valor and wanted him as a general, but first put him in chains in prison.

sentences.zh: 久之，梁主遣人誘之，君立曰：「敗軍之將，難與議勇，如欲將我，我雖真誠效命，能信我乎？

translations.literal: After a long while the Liang ruler sent men to entice him. Junli said, "A defeated army's commander is hard to discuss valor with. If you wish to make me a general, though I would serve you in true sincerity, could you trust me?
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval the Liang ruler sent envoys to win him over. Junli said, "A beaten commander is a poor partner in talk of courage. Even if I meant to serve you honestly, would you trust me?

sentences.zh: 人皆有君，吾何忍反為仇人哉！

translations.literal: Every man has his lord—how could I bear to turn and serve my enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Every man has his sovereign—how could I face my own as an enemy's officer?

sentences.zh: 」既而諸將被戮，尚惜君立不之害。

translations.literal: " Thereafter the other generals were executed, yet they still spared Junli and did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: " Other captives were executed, but they still spared Junli.

sentences.zh: 同光元年，莊宗至汴前一日，梁主始令殺之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongguang, on the day before the Emperor Zhuangzong reached Bian, the Liang ruler at last ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang year 1, the day before Zhuangzong entered Bian, the Liang ruler finally had him executed.

sentences.zh: 高行珪，燕人也。

translations.literal: Gao Xinggui was a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xinggui was from Yan.

sentences.zh: 家世勇悍，與弟行周俱有武藝，初仕燕為騎將，驍果出諸將之右。

translations.literal: His family for generations was fierce and valiant; he and his younger brother Xingzhou both had martial skill. He first served Yan as a cavalry officer, fierce and outstanding above the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was famed for fierceness; he and his brother Xingzhou were both skilled fighters. He first served Yan as a cavalry officer and outshone his peers.

sentences.zh: 燕帥劉守光僭逆不道，莊宗令周德威征之，守光大懼，以行珪為武州刺史，令張犄角之勢。

translations.literal: The Yan commander Liu Shouguang acted with usurping impropriety; the Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Zhou Dewei to campaign against him. Shouguang was greatly afraid and made Xinggui prefect of Wu, ordering him to spread a pincer position.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan ruler Liu Shouguang rebelled, Zhuangzong sent Zhou Dewei against him. Shouguang in fear made Xinggui prefect of Wu to hold a flank.

sentences.zh: 時明宗將兵助德威平燕，俄聞行珪至，率騎以禦之。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor Mingzong was leading troops to help Dewei pacify Yan; soon he heard Xinggui had arrived and led cavalry to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was then assisting Dewei; hearing Xinggui was near, he rode out to confront him.

sentences.zh: 明宗諭以逆順之理，行珪乃降。

translations.literal: The Emperor Mingzong instructed him in the logic of rebellion and obedience, and Xinggui thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong explained loyalty and rebellion; Xinggui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 守光將元行欽在山北，聞行珪有變，即率部下軍眾以攻行珪。

translations.literal: Shouguang's general Yuan Xingqin was north of the mountains; hearing Xinggui had changed sides, he immediately led his troops to attack Xinggui.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang's officer Yuan Xingqin was in the northern hills; learning of the defection, he marched on Xinggui at once.

sentences.zh: 行珪遣弟行周告急於周德威，德威命明宗、李嗣本、安金全將兵援之。

translations.literal: Xinggui sent his younger brother Xingzhou to Zhou Dewei in urgent appeal; Dewei ordered the Emperor Mingzong, Li Siben, and An Jinquan to lead troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui sent Xingzhou to Zhou Dewei for help; Dewei sent Mingzong, Li Siben, and An Jinquan to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 明宗破行欽於廣邊軍，行欽亦降。

translations.literal: The Emperor Mingzong defeated Xingqin at Guangbian Army, and Xingqin also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong routed Xingqin at Guangbian and took his surrender too.

sentences.zh: 尋以行珪為朔州刺史，曆忻、嵐二郡，遷雲州留後。

translations.literal: Soon Xinggui was made prefect of Shuo, passed through the two prefectures of Xin and Lan, and was transferred to acting governor of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Shuo, then served Xin and Lan, and became acting governor of Yun.

sentences.zh: 天成初，授鄧州節度使，尋移鎮安州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was made military governor of Deng Prefecture and soon transferred to garrison An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng he received Deng as his circuit and was soon moved to An.

sentences.zh: 行珪性貪鄙，短於為政，在安州日，行事多不法。

translations.literal: Xinggui's nature was greedy and base, and he was deficient in governing; in his days at An Prefecture his conduct was often unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui was grasping and a poor administrator; at An his rule ran routinely outside the law.

sentences.zh: 副使範延策者，幽州人也，性剛直，累為賓職，及佐行珪，睹其貪猥，因強諫之，行珪不從。

translations.literal: His vice commissioner Fan Yance was a man of Youzhou, upright by nature, who had repeatedly served as a staff officer. When he assisted Xinggui and saw his greed and baseness, he strongly remonstrated, but Xinggui would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Fan Yance, a blunt Youzhou man who had served many posts, saw the corruption and pressed him hard; Xinggui ignored him.

sentences.zh: 後延策因入奏，獻封章於闕下，事有三條：一請不禁過淮豬羊，而禁絲綿匹帛，以實中國；

translations.literal: Later Yance entered court to memorialize and presented a sealed memorial at the palace, with three items: first, request not to forbid pigs and sheep crossing the Huai but to forbid silk and cloth, to enrich the central lands;
translations.idiomatic: Later Fan went to court with a sealed memorial in three parts: first, stop banning pigs and sheep south of the Huai but ban silk exports to enrich the heartland;

sentences.zh: 一請於山林要害置軍鎮，以絕寇盜；

translations.literal: second, request to place military posts at vital points in mountains and forests to cut off bandits;
translations.idiomatic: second, post garrisons at mountain passes to choke banditry;

sentences.zh: 一述藩侯之弊，請敕從事明諫諍之，不從，令諸軍校列班廷諍。

translations.literal: third, set forth the abuses of frontier lords, requesting an edict that staff officers speak plainly in remonstrance, and if not heeded, that military officers line up in court to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: third, describe the failings of military governors and order staff to remonstrate openly, with officers lined in court if ignored.

sentences.zh: 行珪聞之，深銜之。

translations.literal: When Xinggui heard of it he deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggui hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 後因戍兵作亂，誣奏延策與之同謀，父子俱戮於汴，聞者冤之。

translations.literal: Later, because garrison soldiers mutinied, he falsely memorialized that Yance had plotted with them, and father and son were both executed at Bian; those who heard it deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison troops mutinied he accused Fan of complicity; father and son were executed at Bian, and listeners called it a frame.

sentences.zh: 未幾，行珪以疾卒。

translations.literal: Before long Xinggui died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 張廷裕，代北人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Tingyu was a man of the northern Dai region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingyu came from the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 幼事武皇於雲中，從平黃巢，討王行瑜，自行間漸升為小將。

translations.literal: In youth he served the Martial Emperor at Yunzhong, followed in pacifying Huang Chao and campaigning against Wang Xingyu, and from the ranks gradually rose to junior commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Martial Emperor at Yunzhong as a youth, fought Huang Chao and Wang Xingyu, and rose from the ranks to junior commander.

sentences.zh: 莊宗定魏，補天雄軍左廂馬步都虞候，曆蔚、慈、隰三州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Zhuangzong secured Wei he was made left-wing horse-and-foot commandant of the Tianxiong Army and successively served as prefect of the three prefectures Wei, Ci, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong took Wei he became left-wing commandant of Tianxiong cavalry and infantry, then held Wei, Ci, and Xi in turn.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，除新州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was made military governor of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang year 3 he was made military governor of Xin.

sentences.zh: 塞上多事，廷裕無控製之術，邊鄙常聳。

translations.literal: The frontier was troubled; Tingyu lacked methods of control, and the borderlands were often alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was unsettled; Tingyu could not steady it, and the marches stayed on edge.

sentences.zh: 天成三年，卒於治所。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he died at his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 3 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太保。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 王思同，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Wang Sitong was a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sitong came from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 父敬柔，曆瀛、平、儒、檀、營五州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jingrou successively served as prefect of the five prefectures Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingrou had been prefect of Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and Ying in succession.

sentences.zh: 思同母即劉仁恭之女也，故思同初事仁恭為帳下軍校。

translations.literal: Sitong's mother was the daughter of Liu Rengong; therefore Sitong at first served Rengong as a camp officer under his tent.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Liu Rengong's daughter, so Sitong first served Rengong as a tent guard.

sentences.zh: 會劉守光攻仁恭於大安山，思同以部下兵歸太原，時年十六，武皇命為飛騰指揮使。

translations.literal: When Liu Shouguang attacked Rengong at Da'an Mountain, Sitong led his subordinate troops to Taiyuan; he was sixteen, and the Martial Emperor appointed him commander of the Soaring Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouguang besieged Rengong at Da'an Mountain, Sitong brought his men to Taiyuan at sixteen; the Martial Emperor made him commander of the Soaring Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗平定山東，累典諸軍。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor Zhuangzong in pacifying Shandong and repeatedly directed various armies.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong in pacifying Shandong and held a series of commands.

sentences.zh: 思同性疏俊，粗有文，性喜為詩什，與人唱和，自稱薊門戰客。

translations.literal: Sitong's nature was open and handsome, with some rough literacy; he delighted in composing verse and exchanging poems with others, styling himself the Battle Guest of Jimen.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong was easy and quick-witted, literate enough to versify, traded poems freely, and called himself the Battle Guest of Jimen.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌待之若子。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji treated him like a son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wei Jiji treated him almost as family.

sentences.zh: 時內養呂知柔侍興聖宮，頗用事，思同不平之。

translations.literal: At that time the inner attendant Lü Zhirou attended the Xingsheng Palace and wielded considerable power; Sitong resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Lü Zhirou held sway at the Xingsheng Palace; Sitong despised him.

sentences.zh: 呂為終南山詩，末句有「頭」字，思同和曰：「料伊直擬衝霄漢，賴有青天壓著頭。

translations.literal: Lü wrote a poem on Mount Zhongnan whose closing line had the character "head"; Sitong replied in rhyme, "I reckon he means to pierce the heavens—thank heaven a blue sky presses on his head.
translations.idiomatic: Lü wrote a Zhongnan poem ending in "head"; Sitong answered, "He aims to pierce the sky—lucky the blue heaven weighs on his head.

sentences.zh: 」其所為詩句，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " The verses he composed were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: " His verses ran to that sharp tone.

sentences.zh: 每從征，必在興聖帳下，然同光朝，位止鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed campaigns he was always under the Xingsheng tent, yet in the Tongguang reign his rank stopped at prefect of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under the Xingsheng banner, yet through the Tongguang era never rose above prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 明宗在軍時，素知之，即位後，用為同州節度使，未幾，移鎮隴右。

translations.literal: The Emperor Mingzong had known him well in the army; after he took the throne he used him as military governor of Tong Prefecture, and before long transferred him to garrison Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong knew him from the campaigns; on accession he gave him Tong, then moved him to Longyou.

sentences.zh: 思同好文士，無賢不肖，必館接賄遺，歲費數十萬。

translations.literal: Sitong loved literati; whether worthy or base he would lodge and entertain them with gifts, spending several hundred thousand a year.
translations.idiomatic: He courted scholars good and bad, housed them, and lavished gifts—tens of thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 在秦州累年，邊民懷惠，華戎寧息。

translations.literal: For many years at Qin Prefecture the border people cherished his kindness, and Chinese and barbarians were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Years at Qin won the border people's affection; Chinese and tribesmen alike kept the peace.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，入朝，見於中興殿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing he entered court and was received at the Zhongxing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing year 1 he came to court and was received in the Zhongxing Hall.

sentences.zh: 明宗問秦州邊事，對曰：「秦州與吐蕃接境，蕃部多違法度。

translations.literal: The Emperor Mingzong asked about Qinzhou frontier affairs. He replied, "Qin Prefecture borders the Tibetans; many Tibetan groups violate regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong asked about the Qinzhou frontier. He said, "Qin borders Tibet; many Tibetan bands break the rules.

sentences.zh: 臣設法招懷，沿邊置寨四十餘所，控其要害。

translations.literal: Your servant devised methods to win them over and placed more than forty stockades along the border to control the vital points.
translations.idiomatic: I won them by policy and set more than forty stockades along the line to hold the passes.

sentences.zh: 每蕃人互市、飲食之界上，令納器械。

translations.literal: Whenever Tibetans traded or ate at the border, I ordered them to surrender weapons.
translations.idiomatic: At every market or meal on the border I required them to hand over arms.

sentences.zh: 」因手指畫秦州山川要害控扼處。

translations.literal: " He thereupon pointed with his finger and sketched the vital controlling points of Qin Prefecture's mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: " He traced Qin's mountains and choke points with his finger on the map.

sentences.zh: 明宗曰：「人言思同不管事，豈及此耶！

translations.literal: The Emperor Mingzong said, "People say Sitong does not attend to affairs—who would have thought it reached this!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "They say Sitong neglects his post—yet see this!

sentences.zh: 」時兩川叛，欲用之，且留左右，故授右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: " At that time the two Sichuan circuits rebelled; the court wished to use him and kept him at court, and therefore made him general of the Right Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: " With Shu in revolt the court meant to use him and kept him at the capital as general of the Right Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 八月，授西南面行營馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was made horse-and-foot commandant of the southwestern campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he became horse-and-foot commandant of the southwestern campaign.

sentences.zh: 九月，遷京兆尹、西京留守。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and defender of the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and defender of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 伐蜀之役，為先鋒指揮使。

translations.literal: In the campaign to attack Shu he was vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shu expedition he commanded the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭入大散關。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang entered Dasan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang pushed through Dasan Pass.

sentences.zh: 思同恃勇先入劍門，大軍未相繼，復被董璋兵逐出之。

translations.literal: Sitong, relying on his courage, entered Jianmen first; the main army had not yet followed in succession, and he was again driven out by Dong Zhang's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong, bold with his own courage, rushed Jianmen ahead of the main host and was thrown back by Dong Zhang.

sentences.zh: 及敬瑭班師，思同以曾獲劍門之功，移鎮山南西道。

translations.literal: When Jingtang withdrew the army, Sitong was transferred to garrison Shannan West Circuit for having once taken Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingtang withdrew, Sitong was moved to Shannan West for his earlier seizure of Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 三年，兩川交兵，明宗慮並在一人，則朝廷難製，密詔思同相度形勢，即乘間用軍，事未行而董璋敗。

translations.literal: In the third year the two Sichuan circuits fought each other; the Emperor Mingzong feared that if both were in one man's hands the court would be hard pressed to control them, and secretly ordered Sitong to survey the situation and seize the moment to use troops. The matter had not been carried out when Dong Zhang was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the two Shu circuits warred on each other; Mingzong feared one man holding both and secretly told Sitong to survey and strike when he could. Dong Zhang fell before the plan moved.

sentences.zh: 八月，復為京兆尹兼西京留守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he again became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and concurrently defender of the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he again became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and defender of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 時潞王鎮鳳翔，與之鄰境，及潞王不稟朝旨，致書於秦、涇、雍、梁、邠諸帥，言：「賊臣亂政，屬先帝疾篤，謀害秦王，迎立嗣君，自擅權柄，以致殘害骨肉，搖動藩垣。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Lu garrisoned Fengxiang on a neighboring border; when the Prince of Lu did not follow the court's orders he sent letters to the commanders of Qin, Jing, Yong, Liang, and Bin, saying, "Rebel ministers have thrown the government into disorder. When the late emperor was gravely ill they plotted to harm the Prince of Qin, installed a successor, and seized power for themselves, bringing injury to the imperial kin and shaking the frontier lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu held Fengxiang on the border; defying court orders he wrote the governors of Qin, Jing, Yong, Liang, and Bin: "Traitors have thrown the realm into chaos. At the late emperor's deathbed they plotted against the Prince of Qin, set up a boy, seized power, harmed the clan, and shook the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 懼先人基業，忽焉墜地，故誓心入朝，以除君側，事濟之後，謝病歸藩。

translations.literal: Fearing that the forefathers' enterprise might suddenly fall to earth, I have sworn to enter court to remove those beside the throne; when the affair is settled I will plead illness and return to my fief.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing our forefathers' work would collapse, I swear to march on court to clear the throne; when it is done I will plead illness and return to my fief.

sentences.zh: 然藩邸素貧。

translations.literal: Yet the princely residence has always been poor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the princely house has always been poor.

sentences.zh: 兵力俱困，欲希國士，共濟急難。

translations.literal: Troops and strength are both exhausted; I wish to look to the state's scholars to share in relieving the urgent peril.
translations.idiomatic: My troops are spent; I ask the empire's loyal men to share the burden.

sentences.zh: 」乃令小伶女十人以五弦技見思同，因歡諷動，又令軍校宋審溫者，請使於雍，若不從命，即獨圖之。

translations.literal: " He then sent ten young female entertainers skilled on the five-string to appear before Sitong and moved him with song and satire; he also sent the military officer Song Shenwen to request an envoy to Yong, and if orders were not obeyed, to act alone.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent ten girl musicians with five-string lutes to Sitong's hall to sway him with song, and the officer Song Shenwen to Yong as envoy—with orders to move alone if Sitong refused.

sentences.zh: 又令推官郝昭、府吏朱延乂以書檄起兵。

translations.literal: He also ordered the push officer Hao Zhao and the yamen clerk Zhu Yanyi to raise troops by written proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the push officer Hao Zhao and clerk Zhu Yanyi with mobilization orders.

sentences.zh: 會副部署藥彥稠至，方宴，而妓、使適至，乃擊之於獄。

translations.literal: When the deputy deployment Yao Yanchou arrived, a banquet was in progress and the entertainers and envoy happened to come; they were seized and cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Yao Yanchou arrived during a feast just as the entertainers and envoy came; Sitong threw them all into prison.

sentences.zh: 彥稠請誅審溫，拘送昭赴闕。

translations.literal: Yanchou requested execution of Shenwen and sent Zhao under guard to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou asked to execute Shenwen and sent Zhao to court under guard.

sentences.zh: 時思同已遣其子入朝言事，朝廷嘉之，乃以思同為鳳翔行營都部署，起軍營於扶風。

translations.literal: At that time Sitong had already sent his son to court to report affairs; the court praised this and therefore made Sitong overall deployment of the Fengxiang campaign army, raising a camp at Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong had already sent his son to court with a report; the court approved and made him overall deployment against Fengxiang, encamping at Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 三月十四日，與張虔釗會於岐下，梯衝大集。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the third month he joined Zhang Qianjie at Qi; siege towers and rams were massed.
translations.idiomatic: On the third month's fourteenth day he joined Zhang Qianjie below Qi; siege engines crowded the field.

sentences.zh: 十五日，進收東西關城，城中戰備不完，然死力禦捍，外兵傷夷者十二三。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth they advanced and took the eastern and western pass cities. The city's war preparations were incomplete, yet they defended with desperate force; of the outer troops one or two in ten were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth they took the eastern and western gate towns. Defenses were thin but the garrison fought to the death; one or two in ten of the besiegers were hit.

sentences.zh: 十六日，復進攻其城，潞王登陴泣諭於外，聞者悲之。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth they again pressed the assault on the city; the Prince of Lu mounted the battlements and wept as he addressed those outside, and those who heard were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth they assaulted the wall again; the Prince of Lu stood on the ramparts weeping to the army below, and listeners mourned.

sentences.zh: 張虔釗性褊，詰旦，西南用軍，與都監皆血刃以督軍士，軍士齊詬，反攻虔釗，虔釗躍馬避之。

translations.literal: Zhang Qianjie was narrow by nature; at dawn he used troops on the southwest and, with the army inspectors, drew blood on their blades to drive the soldiers. The soldiers cursed together and turned to attack Qianjie; Qianjie leaped his horse aside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianjie was harsh; at dawn he drove the southwest wing with inspectors who bloodied their swords on the ranks. The men cursed him and turned on Qianjie, who spurred aside.

sentences.zh: 時羽林指揮使楊思權引軍自西門先入，思同未之知，猶督士登城。

translations.literal: At that time the Feathered Forest commander Yang Siquan led troops in first from the west gate; Sitong did not know it and still drove the men up the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Feathered Forest commander Yang Siquan entered first from the west gate; Sitong, unaware, still pressed men up the ladders.

sentences.zh: 俄而嚴衛指揮使尹暉呼曰：「西城軍已入城受賞矣，軍士可解甲！

translations.literal: Soon the Strict Guard commander Yin Hui shouted, "The western-city troops have entered the city and are receiving rewards—soldiers may lay down arms!
translations.idiomatic: Then Strict Guard commander Yin Hui cried, "The west-gate men are inside taking reward—drop your weapons!

sentences.zh: 」棄仗之聲，振動天地。

translations.literal: " The sound of casting aside weapons shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: " The clatter of discarded arms shook the sky.

sentences.zh: 日午，亂軍畢集，涇州張從賓、邠州康福、河中安彥威皆遁去。

translations.literal: At midday the mutinous troops were all gathered; Zhang Congbin of Jing Prefecture, Kang Fu of Bin Prefecture, and An Yanwei of Hezhong all fled.
translations.idiomatic: By noon the mutineers had massed; Zhang Congbin of Jing, Kang Fu of Bin, and An Yanwei of Hezhong all fled.

sentences.zh: 十七日，思同與藥彥稠、萇從簡俱至長安，劉遂雍閉關不內，乃奔潼關。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth Sitong, together with Yao Yanchou and Chang Congjian, all reached Chang'an; Liu Suiyong closed the passes and would not admit them, and they fled to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth Sitong reached Chang'an with Yao Yanchou and Chang Congjian; Liu Suiyong shut the gates and they fled to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，潞王至昭應，前鋒執思同來獻。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second the Prince of Lu reached Zhaoying; the vanguard seized Sitong and brought him forward.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second the Prince of Lu came to Zhaoying; the vanguard seized Sitong and presented him.

sentences.zh: 王謂左右曰：「思同計乖於事，然盡心於所奉，亦可嘉也。

translations.literal: The prince said to those about him, "Sitong's plans went wrong in the affair, yet he gave his utmost to what he served—this too may be praised.
translations.idiomatic: The prince told his attendants, "Sitong chose badly, yet he gave his all to his lord—that too deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 」顧謂趙守鈞曰：「思同爾之故人，可行迓之於路，達予撫慰之意。

translations.literal: " He turned to Zhao Shoujun and said, "Sitong is your old acquaintance—you may go meet him on the road and convey my intent to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: " He told Zhao Shoujun, "Sitong is your old friend—meet him on the road and give him my reassurance.

sentences.zh: 」思同至，潞王讓之曰：「賊臣傾我國家，殘害骨肉，非予弟之過。

translations.literal: When Sitong arrived, the Prince of Lu reproached him, saying, "Rebel ministers have overturned my state and harmed the imperial kin—it is not my younger brother's fault. I raised troops at Qishan to execute one or two rebel ministers; why did you waver between two sides and mislead me in many ways? Today's guilt—can it be escaped!"
translations.idiomatic: When Sitong came, the prince rebuked him: "Traitors ruined the house and kin—this is not my brother's doing. I marched from Qishan to kill a few traitors; why did you hedge and mislead me from every side? Can today's guilt be escaped!"

sentences.zh: 我起兵岐山，蓋誅一二賊臣耳，爾何首鼠兩端，多方誤我，今日之罪，其可逃乎！

translations.literal: I raised troops at Qishan, intending only to execute one or two rebel ministers; why did you waver between two sides and mislead me in many ways? Today's guilt—can it be escaped!
translations.idiomatic: I marched from Qishan to kill a few traitors—why hedge and mislead me from every side? Can today's guilt be escaped!

sentences.zh: 」思同曰：「臣起自行間，受先朝爵命，秉旄仗鉞，累曆重藩，終無顯效以答殊遇。

translations.literal: Sitong said, "Your servant rose from the ranks, received titles from the former dynasty, bore the regent's staff and battle-axe, and passed through many great fiefs, yet in the end had no outstanding achievement to answer the special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong said, "I rose from the ranks, took titles from the former dynasty, bore the regent's axe through great commands, yet never repaid that grace with clear merit.

sentences.zh: 臣非不知攀龍附鳳則福多，扶衰救弱則禍速，但恐瞑目之後，無麵見先帝。

translations.literal: Your servant is not unaware that to cling to the dragon and phoenix brings much fortune, while to support the declining and save the weak brings swift calamity—but I feared that after I close my eyes I would have no face to meet the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I know clinging to the rising sun wins fortune and propping the fallen brings ruin—yet I feared to close my eyes with no face before the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 釁鼓膏原，縲囚之常分也。

translations.literal: Beating the war drum and anointing the plain—being bound as a prisoner is the constant lot.
translations.idiomatic: War drums on the field, ropes in the camp—that is a soldier's portion.

sentences.zh: 」潞王為之改容，徐謂之曰：「且憩歇。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu changed expression for him and slowly said, "Rest awhile.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's face softened and he said gently, "Rest awhile.

sentences.zh: 」潞王欲用之，而楊思權之徒恥見其面，屢啟劉延朗，言「思同不可留，慮失士心。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Lu wished to use him, but Yang Siquan and his sort were ashamed to see his face and repeatedly told Liu Yanlang, saying, "Sitong must not be kept, lest we lose the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince meant to keep him, but Yang Siquan and the like could not bear to see him and told Liu Yanlang again and again that Sitong must not stay or the army would turn.

sentences.zh: 」又，潞王入長安時，尹暉盡得思同家財及諸妓女，故尤惡思同，與劉延朗亟言之。

translations.literal: " Moreover, when the Prince of Lu entered Chang'an, Yin Hui took all of Sitong's family wealth and courtesans, and therefore especially hated Sitong and spoke urgently of it with Liu Yanlang.
translations.idiomatic: " When the prince entered Chang'an, Yin Hui had seized Sitong's wealth and women and hated him all the more, pressing Liu Yanlang.

sentences.zh: 屬王醉，不待報，殺思同並其子德勝。

translations.literal: When the prince was drunk they did not await report and killed Sitong together with his son Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: While the prince was drunk they killed Sitong and his son Desheng without waiting for word.

sentences.zh: 潞王醒，召思同，左右報已誅之矣。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu awoke he summoned Sitong; those at his side reported he had already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince woke he called for Sitong; attendants said he was already dead.

sentences.zh: 潞王怒延朗，累日嗟惜之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu was angry with Yanlang and for days sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: The prince raged at Yanlang and mourned him for days.

sentences.zh: 及漢高祖即位，詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Later Han took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Later Han took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 索自通，字得之，太原清源人也。

translations.literal: Suo Zitong, courtesy name Dezhi, was a native of Qingyuan in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Zitong, courtesy name Dezhi, came from Qingyuan in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父繼昭，以自通貴，授國子監祭酒致仕。

translations.literal: His father Jizhao, because Zitong had become eminent, was made director of the Directorate of Education and retired.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jizhao, raised by his son's rank, was made director of the Directorate of Education and retired.

sentences.zh: 自通少能騎射，嘗於山墅射獵，莊宗鎮太原時，遇之於野，訊其姓名，即補右番廳直軍使。

translations.literal: Zitong in youth could ride and shoot; once while hunting at a mountain villa, when the Emperor Zhuangzong was prefect at Taiyuan he met him in the wild, asked his name, and immediately appointed him commander of the Right Barracks Direct Army.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he rode and shot well; hunting at a mountain lodge he met Zhuangzong, then prefect at Taiyuan, in the field, gave his name, and was made commander of the Right Barracks Direct Army on the spot.

sentences.zh: 後因從獵，射中走鹿，轉指揮使。

translations.literal: Later, while following a hunt, he shot a running deer and was transferred to commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Later on a hunt he brought down a running deer and was promoted to commandant.

sentences.zh: 佐周德威攻燕軍於涿州，擒燕將郭在鈞。

translations.literal: He assisted Zhou Dewei in attacking Yan troops at Zhuozhou and captured the Yan general Guo Zaijun.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Zhou Dewei at Zhuozhou against Yan forces and captured the Yan general Guo Zaijun.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗定魏博，改突騎指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor Zhuangzong in securing Weibo and was made commander of the Shock Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong in securing Weibo and became commander of the Shock Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，自隨駕左右廂馬軍都指揮授忻州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Mingzong took the throne, from attendant at the imperial left and right wing horse armies he was made prefect of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong acceded, he left the imperial horse guard for the prefecture of Xin.

sentences.zh: 歲餘召還，復典禁兵，領韶州刺史，出為大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled, again directed the forbidden troops, held the prefecture of Shao, and went out as military governor of the Datong Army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned to the palace guard, took Shao, and went out as governor of Datong.

sentences.zh: 累歲移鎮忠武，改京兆尹、西京留守。

translations.literal: For successive years he was transferred to garrison Zhongwu, then was made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and defender of the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later held Zhongwu, then Jingzhao as metropolitan governor and defender of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 楊彥溫據河中作亂，自通率師討平之，授河中節度使。

translations.literal: When Yang Yanwen seized Hezhong and rebelled, Zitong led troops to pacify him and was made military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yanwen rebelled at Hezhong, Zitong crushed him and received Hezhong as his circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋自鄜州入為右龍武統軍。

translations.literal: Soon he entered from Yan Prefecture as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he came in from Yan as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 初，自通既平楊彥溫，代末帝鎮河中，臨事失於周旋，末帝深銜之。

translations.literal: At first, after Zitong had pacified Yang Yanwen and replaced the Last Emperor at Hezhong, in handling affairs he failed in tact and the Last Emperor deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: After he pacified Yang Yanwen and took Hezhong from the Last Emperor, his manners at court offended the Last Emperor, who bore a deep grudge.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket for commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary bracket opens.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：自通至鎮，承安重誨指，籍軍府甲仗數上之，以為從珂私造，賴王德妃居中保護，從珂由是得免。）〉

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When Zitong reached his post he followed An Chonghui's direction, registered the armory weapons and reported the count upward, alleging that Congke had manufactured them privately; relying on Consort De's mediation within the palace, Congke thereby escaped harm.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (《Comprehensive Mirror》: On reaching his post he followed An Chonghui, inventoried the commandery arsenal and reported the tally, claiming Congke had forged arms in secret; Consort De interceded at court and Congke was spared.)〉

sentences.zh: 及末帝即位，自通憂悸求死。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Zitong was anxious and fearful and sought death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor acceded, Zitong lived in dread and longed for death.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年七月，因朝退涉洛，自溺而卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Qingtai, as he withdrew from court and crossed the Luo, he drowned himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai year 1, seventh month, leaving court he crossed the Luo and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 子萬進，周顯德中，曆任方鎮。

translations.literal: His son Wanjin, in the Xiande era of Zhou, successively held frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wanjin, under Zhou's Xiande reign, held several frontier commands.
